newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian bourse to start daily stock trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian bourse to start daily stock trade.

text.p: The 33 most active shares on the Lithuanian stock market are to trade daily from December, a bourse spokeswoman said on Thursday.

The shares comprise the group A listings and are traded on the central market every Tuesday and Thursday. Lithuanian bourse trade is carried on either on the central market or via bloc trades which take place off the exchange on a daily basis.
"We see more investor interest in equities," the spokeswoman told Reuters, explaining the decision to increase the trading sessions.
The A group comprises the central market's 33 most active listings and their progress is tracked by one of three indices the bourse introduced in late October.
Total market turnover in the first 10 months of 1996 rose to 398.39 million litas from 337.96 million litas in the corresponding period last year, a rise of 17.9 percent.
"We see a need for central market trade every day but we do not think that the new trading days will be very active at first," one broker told Reuters.
The stock market in the northernmost Baltic state Estonia already takes place daily while in Latvia trade sessions happen on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
